name: Classic Yellow Layer Cake with Chocolate Frosting
description: A tender yellow butter cake stacked with fudgy chocolate frosting, the centerpiece of the postwar boxed-mix boom.

name: Tunnel of Fudge Bundt Cake
description: A dense chocolate-walnut bundt cake with a molten fudge core that stays gooey even after baking.

name: Hummingbird Cake
description: A spiced banana-pineapple layer cake finished with cream cheese frosting and toasted pecans.

name: Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
description: A warmly spiced carrot cake studded with walnuts and pineapple, capped with tangy cream cheese frosting.

name: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
description: An individual dark chocolate cake with an underbaked center engineered to flow the moment it's cut.

name: Red Velvet Cupcake
description: A cocoa-tinged buttermilk cupcake with a faint tang, crowned with a swoop of cream cheese frosting.

name: Rainbow Drip Cake
description: A tall naked-style layer cake in vivid tinted sponges, finished with a glossy ganache drip built for the camera.

name: Basque Burnt Cheesecake
description: A crustless cheesecake baked hot and fast until the top is deliberately scorched, staying custardy and jiggling at the center.

name: Tres Leches Cake
description: A light sponge soaked in three milks until custardy, topped with whipped cream.

name: Chocoflan
description: A single pan that bakes into two layers: dense chocolate cake on the bottom, silky caramel flan on top, known as the 'impossible cake'.

name: Bizcocho Dominicano
description: A pillowy vanilla-almond cake soaked in fruit syrup and swathed in Dominican-style meringue buttercream.

name: Kladdkaka
description: Swedish 'sticky cake' — a thin, fudgy chocolate cake deliberately underbaked to a gooey center.

name: Medovik
description: A Russian honey cake of thin baked honey layers stacked with sour-cream frosting and rested until soft.

name: Kouign-Amann
description: A Breton laminated pastry cake folded with layers of butter and sugar and caramelized until the exterior shatters.

name: Sachertorte
description: A dense Viennese chocolate cake with a thin layer of apricot jam beneath a dark chocolate glaze.

name: Mawa Cake
description: A Parsi Mumbai bakery cake enriched with mawa (reduced milk solids) and cardamom, denser and milkier than a standard sponge.

name: Pandan Chiffon Cake
description: A featherlight Southeast Asian chiffon cake flavored and colored with pandan leaf, coconut-forward and airy.

name: Basbousa
description: A Levantine semolina cake soaked in orange blossom or rosewater syrup, often studded with almonds.

name: Japanese Soufflé Cheesecake
description: A whipped, meringue-lightened cheesecake baked in a water bath until cloud-like and barely sweet.

name: Castella Cake
description: A Nagasaki honey sponge cake of Portuguese origin, tall, moist, and springy with a golden crumb.

name: St. Louis Gooey Butter Cake
description: A yeasted shortcake base topped with a dense, syrupy butter-and-cream-cheese layer that never fully sets.

name: Brooklyn Blackout Cake
description: A triple-layer dark chocolate cake filled with chocolate pudding and coated in cake crumbs, born from a Brooklyn bakery near the WWII-era Navy Yard blackouts.

name: Lane Cake
description: An Alabama white layer cake filled with a boozy custard of egg yolks, bourbon, pecans, and candied cherries.

name: Malva Pudding
description: A warm, spongy South African baked pudding soaked in a hot buttery apricot-cream sauce until deeply moist.

name: Pavlova
description: A crisp-shelled, marshmallow-centered meringue base piled with whipped cream and passionfruit, at the center of a decades-long naming dispute between Australia and New Zealand.

name: Lamington
description: Cubes of Australian sponge cake dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in desiccated coconut.

name: Black Forest Cake
description: A dark chocolate sponge layered with cherries, whipped cream, and a splash of cherry brandy.

name: Panettone
description: A tall, airy, dome-shaped yeasted sweet bread studded with candied fruit and raisins.

name: Pastel de Nata
description: A custard tart in a flaky, laminated pastry shell, blistered and caramelized on top.

name: Victoria Sponge Cake
description: Two vanilla sponge layers sandwiched with raspberry jam and whipped cream.

name: Guinness Chocolate Cake
description: A dark, moist stout-infused chocolate cake topped with a cream cheese frosting styled like a pint's foam head.

name: Sernik
description: A dense, baked Polish cheesecake made with farmer's cheese, traditionally set on a shortcrust base.

name: Dobos Torte
description: A multi-layer sponge cake filled with chocolate buttercream and crowned with a shatteringly thin caramel top.

name: Revani
description: A semolina cake soaked in citrus syrup until dense and moist, popular across the former Ottoman world.

name: Karydopita
description: A spiced Greek walnut cake soaked in honey syrup, dense and fragrant with cinnamon and clove.

name: Moroccan Orange Almond Cake
description: A flourless cake made from whole boiled oranges and ground almonds, naturally moist and gluten-free.

name: Persian Love Cake
description: A rose- and cardamom-scented almond cake, delicately spiced and topped with pistachios.

name: Mooncake
description: A dense, round pastry with a rich lotus seed filling, traditionally centered around a salted egg yolk.

name: Korean Strawberry Cream Cake
description: A featherlight sponge layered with whipped cream and fresh strawberries, minimally sweetened.

name: Ube Cake
description: A vividly purple Filipino cake flavored with ube (purple yam), moist and lightly coconut-scented.

name: Bánh Bò Nướng
description: A baked Vietnamese honeycomb cake with a distinctively chewy, spongy texture riddled with tiny air pockets.

name: Khanom Chan
description: A steamed Thai layered cake made from alternating thin coconut and pandan batters, traditionally nine layers deep.

name: Lapis Legit
description: An Indonesian spiced layer cake built from dozens of thin, individually baked layers, rich with butter and warm spices.

name: Brazilian Brigadeiro Cake
description: A chocolate sponge covered in thick, fudgy brigadeiro frosting and showered with chocolate sprinkles.

name: Nanaimo Bar
description: A no-bake, three-layer Canadian bar with a coconut-crumb base, custard filling, and chocolate topping.

name: Torta Rogel
description: Thin, crisp Argentine pastry wafers stacked with dulce de leche and crowned with torched Italian meringue.

name: Torta de Mil Hojas
description: A Chilean 'thousand-layer cake' of crisp puff pastry sheets stacked with manjar (dulce de leche).

name: Louise Cake
description: A shortbread base topped with raspberry jam and a baked coconut meringue, cut into squares.

name: Kransekake
description: A towering stack of graduated almond rings, piped together with royal icing to mark major celebrations.

name: Runeberg Torte
description: Small cylindrical Finnish almond-and-rum cakes topped with raspberry jam and a delicate ring of icing.

name: Paris-Brest
description: A ring of choux pastry split and filled with hazelnut praline cream, created to commemorate a Paris–Brest cycling race.

name: Cassata Siciliana
description: A Sicilian sponge cake layered with sweetened ricotta, candied fruit, and a shell of green marzipan and white icing.

name: Baumkuchen
description: A German 'tree cake' built from dozens of thin batter layers roasted on a rotating spit, revealing tree-ring layers when sliced.

name: Linzer Torte
description: Often called the world's oldest known cake recipe, a lattice-topped Austrian tart of spiced nut pastry filled with redcurrant jam.

name: Bolo Rei
description: A Portuguese 'King Cake' ring studded with candied and dried fruit, traditionally baked for the Christmas season.

name: Tarta de Santiago
description: A flourless Spanish almond cake dusted with powdered sugar in the shape of the Cross of Saint James, tied to the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage.

name: Battenberg Cake
description: An English cake of pink and yellow checkered sponge squares, wrapped in a sheet of marzipan.

name: Dundee Cake
description: A Scottish fruit cake studded with dried fruit and citrus peel, traditionally finished with a spiral of whole blanched almonds.

name: Welsh Cakes
description: Small griddle-cooked cakes studded with currants, cooked on a bakestone rather than baked in an oven.

name: Drømmekage
description: A Danish 'dream cake' — a simple vanilla sponge topped with a broiled, caramelized coconut layer.

name: Bublanina
description: A Czech fruit sponge cake, its light batter studded generously with fresh fruit — most often cherries or apricots.

name: Cozonac
description: A rich, braided Romanian sweet bread-cake enriched with eggs and butter, filled with a swirl of walnut or cocoa paste.

name: Kyiv Cake
description: A Soviet-era Ukrainian icon: crisp hazelnut meringue layers filled with buttercream, a beloved gift cake since the 1950s.

name: Garash
description: A Bulgarian chocolate cake of thin walnut-studded layers bound with chocolate cream, one of the country's most iconic desserts.

name: Napoleon Torte
description: A many-layered puff pastry cake filled with vanilla custard cream, a beloved centerpiece across the former Soviet Caucasus and Eastern Europe.

name: Prinsesstårta
description: A Swedish 'princess cake' of sponge, pastry cream, and whipped cream, domed under a shell of pale green marzipan.

name: Merveilleux
description: A Northern French and Belgian 'marvel' — two meringue disks sandwiching whipped cream, coated entirely in chocolate shavings.

name: Appeltaart
description: A tall Dutch apple cake bound with cinnamon-spiced apples and a lattice crust, denser and more custardy than an American apple pie.

name: Zuger Kirschtorte
description: A Swiss layer cake soaked generously in cherry brandy (kirsch), a specialty of the town of Zug since the 1915 Swiss National Exhibition.

name: Bolo de Rolo
description: A tightly spiral-rolled Brazilian cake from Pernambuco, its wafer-thin sponge layers spread with guava paste before rolling.

name: Panetón
description: Peru's version of the Italian panettone, a tall dome of enriched sweet bread studded with candied fruit and raisins — Peru is one of the world's largest per-capita panettone markets, especially at Christmas.

name: Chajá
description: A Uruguayan sponge cake layered with dulce de leche, peaches, and clouds of meringue and whipped cream.

name: Torta Negra
description: A Colombian black cake of dark, rum-soaked dried fruit and molasses, traditionally baked for Christmas.

name: Torta de Guayaba
description: A Cuban guava cake — a soft yellow sponge layered and topped with sweet guava paste and cream cheese frosting.

name: Jamaican Black Cake
description: A dense, dark fruit cake made from dried fruit soaked in rum and wine for weeks or months, central to Jamaican Christmas and wedding tradition.

name: Simnel Cake
description: A light fruit cake topped with a layer of marzipan and eleven marzipan balls, traditionally eaten at Easter in the UK and, via colonial-era influence, in Nigeria.

name: Sfouf
description: A bright yellow Levantine semolina cake flavored with turmeric and anise, popular across Lebanon and the wider Levant.

name: Ma Lai Go
description: A steamed Cantonese sponge cake, a dim sum staple prized for its airy texture and faintly caramelized flavor from brown sugar.

name: Kerala Plum Cake
description: A rum-soaked fruit cake central to Kerala's Christian Christmas tradition, dark with caramelized sugar and dried fruit steeped for weeks.

name: Kek Lapis Sarawak
description: An intricately patterned Malaysian layer cake from Sarawak, built layer by layer into elaborate geometric or floral designs.

name: Melktert
description: A South African custard tart with a delicate cinnamon-dusted milk filling, baked in a thin pastry shell.

name: Koeksisters
description: Twisted, deep-fried Afrikaner dough plunged into cold syrup until sticky-sweet and crisp on the outside.

name: Gateau Patate
description: A Mauritian fried sweet potato and coconut cake, traditionally sold as a street snack during Eid.

name: Sans Rival
description: A Filipino cake of crisp cashew meringue layers bound with French buttercream — its name means 'without rival'.

name: Kue Lapis
description: A steamed Indonesian rainbow layer cake, its distinct colored bands built up one thin steamed layer at a time.

name: Bolo de Fubá
description: A humble Brazilian cornmeal teatime cake, often studded with coconut or a wedge of cheese baked right in.

name: Šakotis
description: A Lithuanian 'tree cake' built by dripping batter onto a rotating spit over an open flame until spiky golden branches form.

name: Kremšnita
description: A Croatian custard cream cake — thick vanilla pastry cream sandwiched between crisp layers of puff pastry.

name: Nazook
description: An Armenian swirled pastry cake filled with a sweet walnut paste, baked until the pattern browns in golden rings.

name: Galaktoboureko
description: A Greek dessert of semolina custard wrapped in crisp phyllo, soaked in citrus-scented syrup once out of the oven.

name: Bizcocho de Ron
description: A Puerto Rican rum cake, deeply soaked and fragrant with vanilla — a holiday-table fixture across the island.

name: Great Cake
description: A Barbadian black rum fruit cake, its dried fruit soaked for weeks and darkened with burnt sugar, central to Christmas and weddings.

name: Vínarterta
description: A tall Icelandic-Canadian layer cake of spiced prune filling between thin cardamom-scented layers, carried abroad by Icelandic immigrants.

name: Trinidad Black Cake
description: Trinidad and Tobago's own rum-and-wine-soaked black fruit cake, a distinct national tradition central to Christmas and weddings.

name: Torta Caprese
description: A flourless Italian chocolate-almond cake from the island of Capri, dense and fudgy with a crackled top.

name: Panforte
description: A dense, chewy spiced fruit-and-nut cake from Siena, cut into thin wedges and dusted with powdered sugar.

name: Bolo de Arroz
description: A Portuguese rice-flour muffin-cake, lightly domed and baked in paper cups, a staple of bakery counters and breakfast tables.

name: Financier
description: A small, dense French cake of browned butter and almond flour, named for its gold-bar shape near the Paris stock exchange.

name: Galette des Rois
description: A French puff pastry cake filled with almond frangipane, baked with a hidden charm inside and eaten for Epiphany.

name: Boterkoek
description: A dense, chewy Dutch butter cake, barely more than butter, sugar, flour, and almond — deliberately simple and deeply buttery.

name: Guglhupf
description: A ring-shaped Austrian yeasted cake, often marbled with cocoa or studded with raisins soaked in rum.

name: Boston Cream Pie
description: Despite the name, a genuine cake — two sponge layers filled with vanilla custard and glazed with dark chocolate, Massachusetts' official state dessert.

name: King Cake
description: A braided, cinnamon-swirled New Orleans cake iced in purple, green, and gold, with a tiny plastic baby hidden inside for Mardi Gras.

name: Smith Island Cake
description: Maryland's official state dessert — eight to twelve improbably thin yellow layers stacked with rich chocolate fudge frosting.

name: Italian Cream Cake
description: A Southern American layer cake (despite its name, not from Italy) studded with pecans and coconut under cream cheese frosting.

name: German Chocolate Cake
description: An American invention named for baker Sam German's mild baking chocolate, not the country — chocolate layers filled with coconut-pecan frosting.

name: Chiffon Cake
description: An American invention from 1927 — vegetable oil in place of butter gives this cake an unusually light, moist crumb that stays soft even cold.

name: Election Cake
description: A colonial-era New England spiced yeasted fruit cake, once baked for Election Day gatherings and enjoying a modern revival.

name: Angel Food Cake
description: A fat-free American sponge leavened entirely by whipped egg whites, prized for its cloud-like, pure white crumb.

name: Clootie Dumpling
description: A Scottish steamed spiced fruit pudding-cake, boiled for hours wrapped in a cloth ('cloot') until dense and dark.

name: Barmbrack
description: An Irish spiced fruit tea loaf, traditionally baked for Halloween with small charms hidden inside to tell each eater's fortune.

name: Makowiec
description: A Polish poppy seed roll cake, its yeasted dough swirled tightly around a dense sweet poppy seed filling for Christmas.

name: Rigó Jancsi
description: A Hungarian chocolate sponge and whipped chocolate cream cake, cut into cubes, named for a real Roma violinist swept up in scandal.

name: M'hanncha
description: A Moroccan coiled 'snake cake' of almond paste rolled in warqa pastry, baked golden and dusted with sugar and cinnamon.

name: Mont Blanc
description: A chestnut cream cake of French origin that became a beloved Japanese patisserie icon, piped into a snowy peak of vermicelli-thin chestnut purée.

name: Bánh Da Lợn
description: A Vietnamese steamed layer cake alternating pandan and mung bean batters, prized for its distinctive chewy-soft texture.

name: Pan de Elote
description: A Mexican fresh corn cake, moist and lightly sweet, often made with whole kernels blended right into the batter.

name: Genoa Cake
description: A British light fruit cake topped with whole almonds, milder and less dense than a traditional Christmas fruit cake.
